title: Transfer-matrix calibration for the one-dimensional Ising model
statement: For N >= 3 periodic spins s_i in {-1,+1}, finite beta >= 0 and real h, define Z_N = sum_s exp(beta sum_(i=1)^N s_i s_(i+1) + h sum_(i=1)^N s_i), with s_(N+1)=s_1. Reproduce the transfer-matrix formula for Z_N and prove that psi(beta,h) = lim_(N->infinity) N^-1 log Z_N exists and is real-analytic in h for each finite beta. Here beta and h are dimensionless parameters; the task concerns this nearest-neighbor model.
source_locator: SRC-MATH-103, Section 3.3, Theorem 3.9 and proof, equations (3.10)-(3.11), pp. 90-92.
status_basis: The theorem and its transfer-matrix proof are present in the inspected author chapter. Reproducing them would be calibration, not a new model solution.
plain_summary: Recover an exact equilibrium formula for a chain of interacting two-state spins and explain why this idealized model has no singularity in the field at finite temperature.
assumptions: The spin space is {-1,+1}^N with N >= 3 and periodic boundary conditions.
Only uniform nearest-neighbor interactions and a uniform real field enter the specified exponential weight.
beta is a finite nonnegative dimensionless coupling and h is a dimensionless real field. A physical field would require a stated conversion convention.
Take N to infinity with beta and h fixed; zero-temperature or joint limits are outside the task.
scope: The one-dimensional nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model with the exact partition function in the statement. No extension to higher dimensions, long-range interactions or materials is implied.
target: A complete transfer-matrix derivation of the finite-volume partition function and limiting pressure, including the analytic domain of the result.
success_criteria: Construct a two-by-two transfer matrix and show that its cyclic product counts each interaction and field contribution exactly once.
Derive the eigenvalue formula and justify passage from the finite trace to the limiting logarithmic pressure.
Prove real analyticity in h for every fixed finite beta >= 0 and show that the zero-field derivative of the pressure vanishes.
Optionally verify the finite-volume identity by exact symbolic enumeration for N=3 through 8; label these checks as supporting checks rather than a proof of the limit.
known_results: Friedli and Velenik's Theorem 3.9 gives the exact pressure; its proof uses a transfer matrix. Section 3.9 records the older origins of the pressure and transfer-matrix calculations.
prerequisites: Distinction between a model parameter and a measured physical quantity
significance: A useful calibration for symbolic statistical mechanics: boundary conditions, parameter conventions, dominant eigenvalues and limiting operations all matter despite the small matrix.

requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Equilibrium Gibbs weights for the stated classical periodic lattice model. The thermodynamic limit holds the finite dimensionless parameters fixed.

steps: Expand the cyclic matrix product and match it term by term to the declared partition function.
Check the characteristic polynomial, eigenvalues and their magnitude ordering throughout the parameter domain.
Review the logarithmic-limit argument and positivity conditions before taking derivatives.
Separate mathematical conclusions from any proposed interpretation as a physical material.
